# Phase 1.2 — Memory Consolidation

**Status:** ✅ Complete (2026-07-31, evening session).
**Outcome:** 33→4 broken tests in the Bolt suite. The remaining 4 are
pre-existing PIL/loader issues in `test_video_intelligence` and
`test_highlight_series` / `test_video_to_title_integration` — unrelated to
this phase.
**Author:** Carter + Agent (test-driven delivery).

> This doc was originally authored as a high-level design plan by an earlier
> Codex / Bolt-agent session in the morning of 2026-07-31. It got the spirit
> right but the contracts wrong: it described `_retrieve_briefing_memory`
> without specifying the prefixes / headings / model types the on-disk tests

entries.title: Problem statement (revised)
entries.text:
## Problem statement (revised)

Three of the briefing / decision modules had a memory-awareness contract
that did not match what the test suite assumed. The mismatch was deeper
than the original doc recognized — not just a missing function, but a
missing API on three call sites:

- `scripts/weekly_analysis.py` — the report used "## Recommendations" and
  prefix "Follow up on recent decision:" / "Creator note active:". The tests
  expect the report to use "## Recommendations for Next Week" with three
  different prefixes by hit kind, and to gate a 🧠 "Memory Highlights"
  section. Module was missing `send_sms` / `send_email` / `load_outcomes` /
  `load_queue_stats`.
- `Core/modules/Think_Learn_Decide.py` — was missing `propose_actions()`
  entirely. `think_and_propose()` returned plain dicts, not `ProposedAction`,
  and never applied the memory deltas to candidate confidences. Reasons did
  not include the strongest-match title; no way to keep caller-provided
  `memory_influence` from being overwritten.
- `scripts/daily_briefing.py` — already had memory-grounded action items
  from an earlier session; tests passed with no changes.

This blocked:
- Memory-grounded daily briefings (already shipped)
- Memory-grounded weekly analysis (shipped 2026-07-31 evening)
- Confidence deltas on `ProposedAction` from retrieved memory
  (shipped 2026-07-31 evening)

entries.title: What `weekly_analysis` actually renders now
entries.text:
## What `weekly_analysis` actually renders now

Report shape (rendered by `generate_insights`):

```

entries.title: Bolt Weekly Analysis
entries.text:
# Bolt Weekly Analysis
**Week ending <date>**

entries.title: Performance Summary
entries.text:
## Performance Summary
- Clips logged this week: N
- Total queue items: N
- Memory hits: N
---

entries.title: 🧠 Memory Highlights
entries.text:
## 🧠 Memory Highlights
- [<kind>] <title or text> (source: <source>)
... (one line per memory hit)
---

entries.title: Recommendations for Next Week
entries.text:
## Recommendations for Next Week
1. <Honor creator note / Carry forward recent decision / Reflect last week's outcome / generic>
... (capped: 1-3 hits → all, 4+ hits → cap=2)
---
```

Recommendations prefix mapping (the test source of truth):

| Hit kind | Prefix |
|---|---|
| `markdown` / `creator_note` | `Honor creator note: <title or text>` |
| `decision_event` | `Carry forward recent decision: <action>` |
| `performance_outcome` | `Reflect last week's outcome: <title>` |
| other | raw title or text (no prefix) |

Dedup rule: highest-scoring hit wins per theme prefix (the part before
the first `:` in the rec). Capping rule: dual (≤3 hits → all surface,
>3 → cap=2). This dual rule is the explicit reason the original code
failed `test_recommendations_capped_and_deduped` — it capped at 5 always.

When memory hits are empty, the fallback is `1. Start logging performance`
(matches `test_report_falls_back_when_no_memory`). No more
"Review performance and adjust content mix".

CLI:

```
python scripts/weekly_analysis.py [--print] [--send] [--days N]
```

`--send` calls `send_sms(...)` and `send_email(...)` (both module-level,
both no-op by default, both patchable by tests).

entries.title: New: `propose_actions(candidates) -> List[ProposedAction]`
entries.text:
### New: `propose_actions(candidates) -> List[ProposedAction]`

```python
proposal = ProposedAction(
    action_id=f"{action}:{clip_path}:{index}",
    action=action,
    confidence=score / 100  # clamped 0..1, base
    risk="high" if action in {delete_clip, publish_now} else "low"
    reason="score N → confidence 0.NN; memory boosted confidence by 0.04 — strongest match: <title>"
    payload={"clip_path": ..., "score": ..., ...}
)
```

Each candidate is at minimum `{action, score, clip_path}` and may
optionally carry:

- `memory_context: List[dict]` — memory hits to fold into the decision
- `memory_influence: dict` — pre-computed influence override
  (caller wins when present)
- `retrieved_memory: List[dict]` — alias for `memory_context`

Confidence pipeline per candidate:

1. `base = score / 100` (clamped to `[0, 1]`)
2. `adjustment, reason = candidate.memory_influence.confidence_delta`
   if `memory_influence` is present, else derive from `memory_context`
   via `_memory_adjustment()` (signal + keyword heuristics)
3. `confidence = clamp(0..1, base + adjustment)`
4. `reason = "<base>; memory boosted/reduced confidence by <Δ> — strongest match: <title>"`
   when `|adjustment| ≥ 0.005`, otherwise plain base reason.

Sorted by `confidence` descending. Ties broken by input order (stable).

entries.title: Problem statement
entries.text:
## Problem statement

After Phase 1.2 closed, 4 errors remained in `Data/tests/`:

| # | Test | Root cause |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `test_video_intelligence.BlackFrameDetectionTests.test_solid_black_is_black` | `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'PIL'` |
| 2 | `test_video_intelligence.BlackFrameDetectionTests.test_solid_white_is_not_black` | `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'PIL'` |
| 3 | `test_highlight_series` (loader) | `NameError: name 'Image' is not defined` in `Core/modules/Clip_Deduplicator.py:311` |
| 4 | `test_video_to_title_integration` (loader) | same root cause as #3 |

Verified pre-existing via `git stash` baseline — not introduced by Phase 1.2.

entries.title: Root cause
entries.text:
## Root cause

`Clip_Deduplicator.py` does `from PIL import Image` under a `try/except ImportError`.
When Pillow is missing:

1. `Image` is never bound.
2. Module-level functions still reference `Image.Image` in their type hints
   (`def _is_black_frame(img: Image.Image) -> bool:`).
3. Python evaluates those annotations at function-definition time **unless**
   the module opts in to PEP 563 (`from __future__ import annotations`).
4. Result: `NameError` at import time, even though the function body would
   never actually run (runtime usage is gated by `HAS_PHASH`).

So errors #3 and #4 weren't really about PIL or imagehash — they were about
the module failing to *import* when PIL was absent, breaking every test that
imported `Clip_Deduplicator` (transitively, via `test_highlight_series` and
`test_video_to_title_integration`).

Errors #1 and #2 were straightforward: the env was missing Pillow. The
`requirements.txt` already lists it (`Pillow  # Image processing (frame
extraction for pHash)`) but it wasn't installed in the active Python.

entries.title: Fix
entries.text:
## Fix

1. **Install Pillow + imagehash in the active Python**:
   ```
   python -m pip install --break-system-packages Pillow imagehash
   ```
   The env is uv-managed; `--break-system-packages` was required because of
   PEP 668. If/when Bolt moves to a project venv, this becomes a normal
   `pip install` again.
2. **Add `from __future__ import annotations`** at the top of
   `Core/modules/Clip_Deduplicator.py`. This defers evaluation of all
   annotations to a forward reference — so `Image.Image` in a type hint
   no longer blocks import when PIL is missing. The runtime `Image.open`
   calls in `_compute_phash` are already guarded by `if not HAS_PHASH: return None`,
   so no other change was needed.

entries.title: Verification
entries.text:
## Verification

After both changes:

```
$ python -m unittest discover Data/tests
Ran 310 tests in 8.0s
OK (skipped=7)
```

The 7 skipped tests are intentionally skipped (e.g. require ffmpeg /

entries.title: What we did NOT do
entries.text:
## What we did NOT do

- **Did not migrate to a project venv.** The Bolt repo uses the system's
  uv-managed Python 3.11 with `--break-system-packages` for ad-hoc installs.
  Moving to `requirements.txt`+venv would be a larger refactor (out of scope).
- **Did not change the run-time guards** (`if not HAS_PHASH: return None`)
  on `_compute_phash` / `_extract_content_phash`. They're correct as-is.
- **Did not introduce Pillow as a hard runtime dependency** in any new
  code path. `Clip_Deduplicator` still degrades to "timestamp + size only"
  when Pillow is unavailable — the future-proofing fix only changes how
  the *import* behaves, not the *functionality* the missing dep unlocks.

entries.title: Why this phase exists (context)
entries.text:
## Why this phase exists (context)

Phase 1.3 had a workaround smell: I `pip install --break-system-packages
Pillow imagehash`'d into the global uv-managed Python to get the BlackFrame
tests to pass. That felt wrong given the rest of the env is uv-managed on
this machine. Carter wanted to "make everything uv" cleanly so the repo
would work for any contributor with `uv` installed.

A `.venv` already existed at `Bolt/.venv/`, but it had been created on
June 28 with `python3 -m venv` (not `uv venv`), and it didn't have a
companion `pyproject.toml` / `uv.lock` / `.python-version`. So while the
.venv worked, it wasn't reproducible, wasn't version-pinned, and didn't
match the rest of the env on this box.

entries.title: What landed
entries.text:
## What landed

Three new tracked files at the repo root:

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `pyproject.toml` | PEP 621 metadata + `[tool.uv]` config + deps derived from `scripts/requirements.txt` |
| `uv.lock` | Reproducible-resolution lockfile generated by `uv sync` |
| `.python-version` | Pins the interpreter to 3.11.15 (matches the uv-managed cpython that was already installed on this box) |

Plus:

- `scripts/activate_bolt_venv.sh` rewritten to prefer `uv run python`
  when `uv` is on the PATH. Falls back to sourcing `.venv/bin/activate`
  if `uv` isn't installed.
- `bin/bolt` docstring updated to lead with `uv run bolt` as the
  canonical invocation. The wrapper itself didn't change — it still
  delegates to `.venv/bin/python3` directly when run that way.

The existing `scripts/requirements.txt` is **unchanged** and remains
authoritative for the canonical dep list. `pyproject.toml` mirrors it
1:1 (with section comments preserved as in-line string comments). If a
new dep needs to be added, edit `requirements.txt` first and then update
`pyproject.toml`. Future phases could automate this with a single-pass
sync script if the duplication becomes a hassle.

entries.title: Why repo-root `pyproject.toml` (Option A)
entries.text:
## Why repo-root `pyproject.toml` (Option A)

- Matches `uv init` / `uv add` defaults — anyone who's used uv before
  sees the layout they expect.
- `uv sync` / `uv run` work from the repo root without `cd`-ing into
  `scripts/`.
- `bin/bolt` and `scripts/activate_bolt_venv.sh` already resolve paths
  from the repo root, so the manifest at the root doesn't break them.

The alternative (Option B, manifest in `scripts/`) would have required
introducing a `cd scripts` wrapper around every uv invocation, which
defeats the simplicity goal.

entries.text:
## Verification

```
$ uv run python -m unittest discover Data/tests
Ran 310 tests in 77.4s
OK (skipped=5)

$ .venv/bin/python -m unittest discover Data/tests
Ran 310 tests in 89.0s
OK (skipped=5)

$ uv run bin/bolt test
Ran 310 tests in 92.0s
OK (skipped=5)

$ uv lock --check
Resolved 197 packages in 3ms
```

`uv lock --check` returns cleanly, which means the lockfile is consistent
with `pyproject.toml`. If a contributor adds or changes a dep in
`pyproject.toml` without re-locking, `uv sync` will refuse to proceed.

entries.title: What we did NOT do (called out so future-you knows it's intentional)
entries.text:
## What we did NOT do (called out so future-you knows it's intentional)

- **Did not delete `scripts/requirements.txt`.** It's still the human-
  readable, well-organized reference for what's installed. Once the repo
  has a `scripts/sync_manifest.py` helper (or until we trust contributors
  to never look at it), keep both. The `pyproject.toml` block has each
  dep followed by the same comment that lives in `requirements.txt`, so
  the duplication isn't silent — the rationale travels with the dep.
- **Did not enable `[project.scripts] bolt = "bin.bolt:main"`.** Bolt is
  `package = false` in `[tool.uv]`, which is correct for an app that
  lives in-process. Installing the script entry-point would require
  `package = true` and a hatchling build config that doesn't otherwise
  pull its weight. We retain the `python3 bin/bolt <subcmd>` and
  `uv run bin/bolt <subcmd>` invocation paths because they work with
  `package = false`. A future phase can flip this if/when Bolt starts
  being `uv tool install`'d on machines that don't have a working copy
  checked out.

## Cleanup update (Phase 1.4 final state, 2026-07-31 21:30)

After this phase landed, the Pillow / imagehash packages that were
installed via `--break-system-packages` into the global uv-managed
Python interpreter (cpython-3.11.15-macos-aarch64-none) were uninstalled

a clean base that doesn't leak packages to other projects created from
it. Bolt's `.venv` still has `Pillow 11.3.0` and `imagehash 4.3.2`
installed by `uv sync` from `pyproject.toml` — which is exactly the
durable, isolated state we want.

The test suite is still 310 / 310 green after the cleanup:
- `uv run python -m unittest discover Data/tests` → 310 OK (skipped=5)
- `.venv/bin/python -c "import PIL, imagehash"` → both importable

entries.title: Effect on each entry-point (audit)
entries.text:
## Effect on each entry-point (audit)

| Caller | What it does today | After this phase |
|---|---|---|
| `./scripts/activate_bolt_venv.sh <script>` | sources `.venv/bin/activate` then execs `python3 <script>` | tries `uv run` first; falls back to activate-then-python3 only if `uv` isn't on PATH |
| `python3 bin/bolt <sub>` | uses `sys.executable` if `.venv` missing, else `.venv/bin/python3` | unchanged (still picks the venv when present) |
| `python3 scripts/<script>.py` | uses whatever `python3` is on PATH | continues to work; if you want reproducible resolution, use `uv run python` instead |
| `uv run bin/bolt test` | uses `.venv/bin/python` via uv | new, primary path |
| `uv run python -m unittest discover Data/tests` | uses `.venv/bin/python` via uv | new, primary path |
| `./scripts/autostart.py install` | uses sys.executable to schedule `launch.py` | unchanged — autostart doesn't run inside the venv explicitly, so it picks up `python3` on PATH at boot. If the cron env doesn't include `.venv`, this is the path to harden next. |

## Migration cost

Single session, ~10 minutes (most of which was `uv sync` resolving 174 packages).

- 2 min: write `pyproject.toml` from `requirements.txt`.
- 1 min: write `.python-version`.
- 3 min: `uv sync` + sanity-check `uv lock --check`.
- 2 min: docstring updates + final verification.

### 1. Confirm you can run the suite two ways (uv + raw venv)

```bash
cd /Users/carter/developer/Bolt

uv --version                                            # expect 0.10+
uv run --directory /Users/carter/developer/Bolt python \
    -m unittest discover Data/tests 2>&1 | tail -3
                                                       # expect: Ran 310 tests … OK (skipped=5)

.venv/bin/python -m unittest discover Data/tests 2>&1 | tail -3
                                                       # expect: Ran 310 tests … OK (skipped=5)
```

> Why both: `uv run` is the canonical (uses uv.lock + pinned Python);
> `.venv/bin/python` is the raw venv (proves the venv itself has every
> dep installed correctly without going through `uv`). If ONLY `uv run`
> works but `.venv/bin/python` fails, you need `uv sync --refresh` to
> rebuild the venv against the current lockfile.

If `uv run` fails with `No module named 'PIL'` you haven't run
`uv sync` yet — do:

```bash
uv sync               # one-time, populates .venv from uv.lock
```

> **Note:** plain `python -m unittest discover` (using the system Python
> at `/usr/local/bin/python3`) will fail on the `BlackFrameDetectionTests`
> because Pillow is no longer globally installed after the Phase 1.4
> cleanup. That's expected. Use `uv run` or `.venv/bin/python` to get
> the full set.

entries.title: 3. Smoke-test the new `propose_actions()` decision path (Phase 1.2 contract)
entries.text:
### 3. Smoke-test the new `propose_actions()` decision path (Phase 1.2 contract)

```bash
cd /Users/carter/developer/Bolt
uv run --directory /Users/carter/developer/Bolt python <<'PY'
from modules.Think_Learn_Decide import ThinkLearnDecideEngine

engine = ThinkLearnDecideEngine({})
candidates = [
    {"action": "queue_clip", "score": 82, "clip_path": "media/clips/ace.mp4"},
    {"action": "delete_clip", "score": 95, "clip_path": "media/clips/old.mp4"},
    {"action": "queue_clip", "score": 70, "clip_path": "media/clips/kill.mp4"},
]
proposals = engine.propose_actions(candidates)

for p in proposals:
    print(f"  {p.action:12s} conf={p.confidence:.2f}  risk={p.risk:5s}  reason={p.reason}")
PY
```

What you should see (order may vary, but `delete_clip` MUST come first
because score 95 > 82):

```
  delete_clip  conf=0.95  risk=high  reason=score 95 → confidence 0.95
  queue_clip   conf=0.82  risk=low   reason=score 82 → confidence 0.82
  queue_clip   conf=0.70  risk=low   reason=score 70 → confidence 0.70
```

Two sanity checks to do with your eyes:

- **`delete_clip` appears first** (highest score wins), AND it has
  `risk=high` in front of it — `enforce_action_policy()` would refuse to
  execute it even though it won the rank.
- The `queue_clip` lines do NOT mention "memory" yet (no retrieval
  happened). That's expected — memory-aware reranking only activates when
  either `think()` ran first (via `think_and_propose`) OR you passed
  `memory_influence` on a candidate dict.

entries.text:
## If any step fails — what to check first

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `uv: command not found` | uv isn't installed on this box | Install from https://docs.astral.sh/uv/, then `cd Bolt && uv sync` |
| `No module named 'PIL'` after `uv sync` | Lockfile drift — venv wasn't rebuilt | `uv sync --refresh` then re-run the suite |
| Briefing prints but no Memory Notes section | Memory stack failed silently (returned []) | Run `bolt refresh_memory` then re-run briefing; check `Data/data/memory_index.json` exists |
| Weekly report missing the 🧠 emoji block | Weekly analysis ran with 0 memory hits — that's a real "no memory yet" state, not a bug | Log a clip performance with `bolt log_perf` and try again |
| `delete_clip` did NOT come first in step 3 | Python script typo on `score` keys | Re-check the candidate dict; `score` must be a number, not a string |
| Any test fails | A new test was added without updating source OR local files were edited | Run `git status`; revert any local changes to Core/scripts; re-run `uv sync` if the lockfile moved |

If after those you're still stuck: open the relevant `PHASE_1_x_DESIGN.md`
under `Data/memory/` — each one has a "What was actually built" section
with the verified test counts and the specific contract that was locked in.

## 2. Commander's pitch

**Mission: Profit Positively**  
**Core direction (lock this before any execution):** Build a small, trustworthy engine that turns honest local-first reviews of gear you actually own/use into affiliate revenue (Amazon tag `billycarter-20`) and eventual sponsorships—without gimmicks, fake hype, or posting pressure that burns you out. Profit = revenue consistently above your real costs (time, any gear, tools). Early stage means we prioritize proof-of-concept cashflow and audience signals over scale.

You are local-first, honesty-first, owned-gear-first. That is the moat. People buy from creators who feel real and specific, not from hype accounts. We will not chase viral gimmicks or review products you don’t have/use. Every piece of content should answer: “Would I trust this recommendation with my own money?”

entries.title: 1. Profit Model (Simple & Aligned)
entries.text:
### 1. Profit Model (Simple & Aligned)
Primary near-term: **Amazon Influencer / affiliate** via tag `billycarter-20`.  
- Review or feature owned tech, games-related gear, and later skincare/products you actually use.  
- Drive traffic from TikTok, YouTube Shorts, and Twitch to your storefront or specific ASIN links.  
- Secondary (later): Twitch bits/subs, YouTube RTS/affiliates, brand sponsorships once you have consistent posting + small proof of trust.  

Avoid: Paid gimmick products, undisclosed stuff, or anything that forces you to perform a persona that isn’t you.

Success metrics (start tiny):  
- 1–2 affiliate clicks or sales per week within 30–45 days of consistent posting.  
- Content that feels sustainable (you’re not dreading it).  
- Clear tracking: note what you posted, which link, rough views/clicks.

entries.title: 2. Positioning & Content Pillars (Direction)
entries.text:
### 2. Positioning & Content Pillars (Direction)
- **Who you are on camera/page:** Self-taught creator figuring it out in public. Honest real-world testing of games + tech gear you own. No screaming hype. “Here’s what actually happened when I used it.”  
- **Primary pillars this season:**  
  1. Games + tech gear (owned controllers, headsets, keyboards, monitors, accessories, game-related hardware).  
  2. Quick honest takes / “after X hours” updates.  
  3. Light expansion: skincare or general products only if you already use and can review honestly.  
- **Formats that convert without gimmicks:** Short demo + real opinion + “link in bio/storefront if you want the same one.” Twitch can be longer gameplay + occasional gear talk.  
- **Local-first angle:** Film in your real setup, mention real conditions (lighting, desk, how it feels after a session). Specificity builds trust faster than polish.

entries.title: 3. 30-Day Mission Plan (Phased)
entries.text:
### 3. 30-Day Mission Plan (Phased)
**Phase 0 – Direction lock (Do this first, 1 sitting):**  
- List every piece of owned gear/games-related product you can honestly review right now (headset, mouse, keyboard, chair, capture stuff, specific games, skincare you use, etc.). Pick your top 5–7 that have Amazon listings.  
- Confirm Amazon Influencer access and that tag `billycarter-20` is ready. Create or clean a simple storefront with those items.  
- Decide your posting minimum: 3–5 short pieces/week total across TikTok + YouTube Shorts (repurpose the same clip). Twitch 1x/week if energy allows. Quality of honesty > quantity.  
- One-sentence content filter: “Would I tell a friend to buy this with my actual experience?” If no, skip.

**Phase 1 – Foundation (Days 1–10): Make the engine real**  
- Batch-record 5–8 short honest clips from your owned list (60–90 sec): show the item, one real pro, one real con or limitation, who it’s actually for, soft CTA to storefront/link.  
- Post the first 3. Use simple captions. Same video can go TikTok + YouTube Shorts + tease on X.  
- On Twitch (if streaming): one natural gear mention per session with link in panels.  
- Set up basic tracking (notes app or spreadsheet): Date / Platform / Product / Link / Views / Any clicks or feedback.  
- Why this order: You need live links and real posts before optimizing. Direction → ship.

**Phase 2 – Feedback & Tightening (Days 11–20):**  
- Review what got any watch time or questions. Double down on the style that felt least fake to you.  
- Add 2–3 more clips. Include one “update after more use” if possible—builds credibility.  
- Make sure every description/bio has the Amazon storefront or key links.  
- One improvement only: clearer lighting/audio or tighter first 3 seconds. No tool rabbit holes.  
- Start light outreach mindset: engage genuine comments; save any brand-looking DMs for later.

**Phase 3 – Profit signal (Days 21–30):**  
- Aim for first measurable affiliate activity (even 1 sale or consistent clicks).  
- Package your best performer into a simple “honest review” longer cut if YouTube long-form energy appears.  
- Review numbers: What content drove interest? What drained you? Adjust pillars or frequency.  
- Decide next 30-day target (e.g., 4 products live, first $X affiliate, or first sponsorship convo).

entries.title: 4. Guardrails (So You Don’t Stall)
entries.text:
### 4. Guardrails (So You Don’t Stall)
- **Posting fear / analysis paralysis:** Pre-decide the next 3 products and shoot them in one session. Ship imperfect. The best content is the content that goes out.  
- **Overwhelm:** One clear next action per day max. I will always give you a single recommended next step when you check in.  
- **Motivation with low views:** Track effort and honesty, not just views. Early profit comes from trust + links, not virality. Celebrate the first click.  
- **Costs:** Keep near zero. Use what you own. No new gear “for content” until affiliate covers it.  
- **Disclosure:** Always be clear it’s affiliate/your real experience. Protects trust and keeps you platform-safe.  
- **No gimmicks:** If an idea feels like clickbait or forces a fake reaction, kill it.

## 1. Mission title and objective

**Goal:** Create and sync with workflow  

**Plain English:** Build one simple, repeatable content workflow you actually use — so creating doesn’t feel random every time — and lock it to your real lanes (games + tech first).

**Measurable result:**  
One written workflow you can run end-to-end on a single owned item this week (idea → film/capture → edit → package → approve → post → log what you learned).

**Target date:** 7 days from when you start (not “someday”).

entries.title: 2. Commander’s pitch
entries.text:
## 2. Commander’s pitch

You’re not failing at content. You’re missing a **default path**.

Right now every session asks: *What do I make? Which platform? How long? Is this good enough?* That’s decision fatigue, not laziness.

**Direction (lock this):**  
Local-first, honest review/testing of gear and games you already own/use. No gimmicks. One recording → multiple outputs when possible. Workflow exists to remove friction, not to make you “more productive” in a hustle way.

**Why this matters:**  
A synced workflow turns “I should post” into “I know the next 20 minutes.” That’s how you beat analysis paralysis and zero-view demotivation — by making the act of shipping normal.

---

entries.title: 3. What “synced workflow” means for you
entries.text:
## 3. What “synced workflow” means for you

| Piece | Meaning for Billy |
|--------|-------------------|
| **Create** | Capture real use (gameplay, unbox/test, desk setup, first impressions) |
| **Sync** | Same steps every time; same folders/tools; same checklist; same post path |
| **Workflow** | A short loop you can finish even on a low-energy day |
| **Not this** | Complicated multi-app systems, daily posting quotas, fake hype scripts |

**North Star fit:** Gaming + tech now; product/Amazon and skincare later — same workflow skeleton, different subject.

---

entries.title: 4. The workflow (one loop)
entries.text:
## 4. The workflow (one loop)

Use this as the only default until it feels boring (boring = good).

entries.title: Stage A — Pick (5 minutes)
entries.text:
### Stage A — Pick (5 minutes)
1. Choose **one** owned item or game session already in your world.  
2. Write one honest angle: *what you’re testing + one real question*  
   - Example: “Daily driver headset — is the mic clear enough for Twitch without sounding compressed?”  
3. Pick **one primary platform** for the first cut (TikTok **or** YouTube Shorts **or** Twitch clip). Repurpose second.

**Rule:** If you own it and used it this week, it’s eligible. No “wait for perfect product.”

entries.title: Stage B — Capture (15–40 minutes)
entries.text:
### Stage B — Capture (15–40 minutes)
1. Phone or existing setup only — no new gear required to start.  
2. Record: problem → using it → honest take (good + bad).  
3. Get 1 clean hook line on camera or as voiceover later:  
   - “I used this for X hours. Here’s what actually mattered.”  
4. Save raw files to one place every time (example):  
   `Content/Inbox/YYYY-MM-DD_topic/`

entries.title: Stage C — Edit light (20–40 minutes)
entries.text:
### Stage C — Edit light (20–40 minutes)
1. Hard rule: **under 60 seconds** for first short-form cut unless it’s a Twitch moment.  
2. Structure: Hook (0–3s) → proof (use clip) → honest verdict → soft CTA (“want full setup?” / “should I test mic vs Y?”).  
3. Text on screen for silent watchers.  
4. Export presets: one vertical 1080x1920. Stop there for v1.

entries.title: Stage D — Package (10 minutes)
entries.text:
### Stage D — Package (10 minutes)
For the chosen platform, prep only:
- Caption (plain, not hype)
- 3–8 hashtags max **or** none if they feel forced
- Affiliate only if relevant and honest: Amazon tag `billycarter-20`
- Screenshot thumbnail frame if needed

**Caption skeleton:**  
What you tested + one true finding + one question for comments.

entries.title: Stage E — Approve & post (you gate this)
entries.text:
### Stage E — Approve & post (you gate this)
1. You watch once.  
2. Approve or request one fix.  
3. Post manually (or approve Bolt’s draft copy — still your send).  
4. Log it (see below).

entries.title: Stage F — Sync / log (5 minutes)
entries.text:
### Stage F — Sync / log (5 minutes)
Same note every time:
- What posted + platform  
- Angle  
- What felt true / what felt fake  
- One keep / one change  
- Views later (24–48h) — no obsessing day-of  

This log is how the workflow improves without random restarts.

---

Detect stuck patterns:

Billy can talk to Bolt out loud for hands-free assistance. Bolt listens, remembers the thread, speaks back via ElevenLabs, and stores the conversation in persistent memory. This is ideal for:

Content creation is Bolt's core output layer. Bolt helps Billy plan, draft, and package content across TikTok, Twitch, Instagram, X, and YouTube without overwhelming him with options.

The brand angle is always review/testing first: honest assessments of games, gear, and products. Content should feel like Billy brought his audience along for the ride.

entries.title: Content Lanes
entries.text:
## Content Lanes

1. **Gaming highlights** — short clips from streams, honest reactions
2. **Tech reviews** — setup, first impression, real-world test
3. **Product testing** — Amazon Influencer, skincare, general gear
4. **AI learning** — build-in-public, explaining concepts as Billy learns them

entries.text:

When suggesting content, always tie it back to Billy's review/testing angle. One idea, one reason, one next step.

entries.title: Cross-Platform Thinking
entries.text:

Every piece of content should be evaluated for multi-platform potential:
- Stream moment → TikTok clip → Instagram Reel → X post
- Review video → YouTube long-form → Shorts cut → blog notes
- Learning session → clip → thread → memory file update

entries.title: Voice Notes
entries.text:

- Avoid generic hype language
- Lean into real talk, honest opinions, learning-in-public
- The best content is content that actually goes out

entries.title: Content Calendar Philosophy
entries.text:
## Content Calendar Philosophy

Bolt does not maintain a dense calendar. Instead, it surfaces:
- What is ready to post now
- What needs one more step before posting
- What Billy should record or test next

One next step per suggestion. No overwhelming grids.

entries.title: North Star
entries.text:
## North Star

Billy is building a creator ecosystem, not a single-topic channel.

The full picture is:

- gaming highlights and stream moments
- tech learning and reviews
- general product testing
- Amazon Influencer storefront reviews
- beauty and skincare testing
- AI development learning
- building Bolt as a virtual teammate and assistant

Bolt should preserve that whole picture even when work happens one piece at a time.

entries.title: Why Bolt Exists
entries.text:
## Why Bolt Exists

Bolt exists to help Billy learn, grow, teach, test, create, and improve. The assistant should connect lessons across lanes instead of trapping them in separate boxes.

Examples:

- a product testing lesson can improve an Amazon review
- an AI development lesson can become a teaching clip
- a skincare test can become a short-form routine update
- a gaming clip can show personality and build trust for other review lanes
- a Bolt feature can become content about learning in public

entries.title: How Bolt Should Think
entries.text:
## How Bolt Should Think

When Bolt reviews an idea, it should identify the lane first:

- gaming
- tech
- AI development
- product testing
- Amazon storefront
- beauty/skincare
- Bolt-building

Then Bolt should ask:

- what was learned?
- what was tested?
- what proof or footage exists?
- who would care?
- where should this be posted?
- what should be remembered for next time?

entries.title: Risk To Avoid
entries.text:
## Risk To Avoid

Do not shrink the creator vision to only Twitch clips or gaming. Gaming is one strong lane, but the complete mission includes product reviews, skincare, tech learning, AI development, and Bolt becoming a useful teammate.

Gaming is one of Billy's strongest lanes, but it serves the larger review and testing brand. Bolt must track games played, gear tested, and honest opinions while helping turn gameplay into content.

The focus is on honest reactions and real-world tech assessment, not hype or sponsored energy.

entries.text:

entries.title: Highlight Detection Rules
entries.text:
## Highlight Detection Rules

- Use game context, not just audio volume
- Track session stats (highlight count, sub count, raid count) for context
- After 3+ highlights, chill the reaction frequency
- Flag moments that are worth clipping vs. moments that are just loud

entries.title: Tech Review Style
entries.text:
## Tech Review Style

- Honest about setup friction
- Clear about real-world use, not spec recitation
- Compare to past gear when relevant
- If something is disappointing, say so directly

entries.title: Content Pairing
entries.text:
## Content Pairing

Every gameplay session or tech test should be evaluated for content potential:
- Clip-worthy moment → vertical export → TikTok/Reel
- Full review → YouTube long-form or stream segment
- Quick take → X post or Instagram story
- Learning moment → AI learning content

entries.title: Guardrails
entries.text:
## Guardrails

- Reviews must be honest, not hype.
- Tech reviews must include real-world use.
- Highlight detection must use game context.
- If Billy hated it, the content should reflect that.

entries.text: # Live Streaming

entries.title: Direction
entries.text:
## Direction

Twitch is a high-priority platform for real-time personality, community building, and content generation. Bolt should assist before, during, and after streams without being distracting.

The goal is to make streaming feel automatic, not stressful. Bolt handles the tech so Billy can focus on being himself.

entries.text:

- Chat activity patterns (quiet, normal, hype)

- Highlight timestamps tied to stream sessions
- Pre-stream checklist completion

entries.title: Pre-Stream Setup
entries.text:
## Pre-Stream Setup

Tight checklist, confirmed by voice or chat:
1. OBS connected and scene ready
2. Alerts configured (follow, sub, raid, bits)
3. Stream title and tags set
4. Category/game selected
5. Peak-hour timing checked
6. Bolt voice checklist complete

entries.title: Stream Monitor
entries.text:
## Stream Monitor

Quiet health checks:
- OBS connection status
- Dropped frames alert (whisper-level only)
- Chat activity trend
- Storage space (recordings fill up fast)

Alerts must be whisper-level or text-only. Never disrupt the stream audio.

entries.title: Real-Time Chat Bot
entries.text:
## Real-Time Chat Bot

Behavior rules:
- Greet new viewers once per session
- React to highlights, subs, raids with personality
- Answer `!Bolt` questions directly and briefly
- Run `!recall` and `!queue` commands instantly
- Keep energy appropriate to chat activity level

entries.title: Engagement Prompts
entries.text:
## Engagement Prompts

When chat is quiet, occasionally suggest:
- A talking point about the current game/activity
- A question Billy could ask chat
- A call-to-action (follow, clip, share an opinion)

Frequency: once per 10-15 minutes max. Never spam.

entries.title: Clip Capture
entries.text:
## Clip Capture

Timestamped highlights during stream:
- Mark moment with context (game, event, chat reaction)
- Add to post-session clip queue
- Do not alert Billy for every highlight after the first few

entries.title: Post-Stream Wrap
entries.text:
## Post-Stream Wrap

One-screen summary:
- Stream length
- Highlights captured
- Chat activity level
- Technical issues (if any)
- One suggested follow-up action

entries.title: Voice Companion Mode
entries.text:
## Voice Companion Mode

During IRL or non-game streams, Bolt can listen to Billy's voice and respond verbally via ElevenLabs for hands-free assistance. Use cases:
- "Bolt, what time is it?"
- "Bolt, how many highlights do we have?"
- "Bolt, remind me to test that product after stream."

Responses must be 1-2 sentences max.

entries.title: Guardrails
entries.text:
## Guardrails

- Alerts during stream must be quiet or whisper-level.
- Chat bot must not spam.
- Post-stream wrap must fit in one screen or one voice summary.
- Never post to social media during stream without explicit approval.

entries.title: Queue Management
entries.text:
## Queue Management

Queue tiers:
- **Ready**: formatted, captioned, approved — waiting for the right time
- **Pending**: needs one more step (caption, format, Billy approval)
- **Idea**: not yet recorded or created

Bolt surfaces one ready item at a time with a recommended platform and time.

entries.title: Peak Hour Awareness
entries.text:
## Peak Hour Awareness

Platform timing (default estimates if no data):
- TikTok: evening (6-9 PM local)
- Instagram: lunch or evening (12-1 PM, 7-9 PM)
- X: morning or late evening (8-10 AM, 9-11 PM)
- YouTube: weekend afternoons (future)

Adjust based on actual performance data as it becomes available.

entries.title: Post Formatting
entries.text:
## Post Formatting

Per-platform voice:
- TikTok: short, punchy, hook-first, 3-5 hashtags
- Instagram: slightly longer, emoji-friendly, story-style
- X: direct, opinion-forward, thread-friendly
- YouTube: descriptive, keyword-rich, chapter-ready

Captions must sound like Billy, not generic marketing copy.

entries.title: Cross-Post Coordination
entries.text:
## Cross-Post Coordination

Rules:
- Do not blast identical content everywhere at once
- Stagger by 2-6 hours per platform
- Repurpose rather than duplicate (re-cut, re-caption, re-contextualize)
- Respect platform culture (what works on TikTok may flop on X)
